# rasuvaeff/yii3-utm

UTM capture and marketing attribution for Yii3. Namespace `Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm`.
PHP 8.3–8.5, requires `ext-json` and `ext-mbstring`.

Status: the core is feature-complete (domain, attribution, capture, config).
The `rasuvaeff/yii3-utm-db` storage adapter is not released yet — until then the
application implements `UtmAttributionRepository` or uses the shipped in-memory
reference implementation.

## Install

```bash
composer require rasuvaeff/yii3-utm
```

## Rules

1. Everything from the client — query, headers, body, cookies, `localStorage` —
   is untrusted. Values are normalised, truncated or dropped, never
   authenticated. Normalisation is not escaping: a value stays arbitrary text
   (`utm_source=<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` survives intact), so escaping at
   the point of output is the consumer's job.
2. `occurredAt` is a claim by the source. It never decides ordering; the server
   assigns order when a row is written, so a late delivery cannot become the
   first touch.
3. One business event produces one row per touchpoint. Idempotency is keyed by
   the event id **and** the touchpoint, not by the event alone.
4. Fingerprints and dedupe keys are derived from the touchpoint. They are never
   constructor arguments — a mismatched fingerprint silently defeats the unique
   index of the journal.
5. Determinism is a storage requirement: `ClickIds` keeps whitelist order,
   `UtmHistory::deduplicated()` keeps the oldest member of a similarity group,
   and history sorting breaks ties by canonical signature. Input-order
   dependence in any of the three writes duplicate rows.
6. A click id without any `utm_*` is a valid touchpoint, not an empty request:
   Google Ads auto-tagging sends a bare `gclid`.

## API reference

### UtmParameters

Campaign tuple. `final readonly`, `@psalm-immutable`.

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\UtmParameters;

$utm = UtmParameters::fromArray([
    'utm_source' => 'google', 'utm_medium' => 'cpc',
    'utm_campaign' => 'summer', 'utm_term' => 'shoes',
    'utm_content' => 'banner-a', 'utm_id' => 'c-42',
]);

new UtmParameters(source: 'google', medium: 'cpc');   // direct construction
$utm->source; $utm->medium; $utm->campaign; $utm->term; $utm->content; $utm->id;
$utm->isEmpty(): bool;
$utm->equals(UtmParameters $other): bool;
$utm->toArray(): array;   // keys: utm_source … utm_id
```

`fromArray()` accepts both `utm_source` and bare `source` (prefixed wins),
strips control characters, trims, truncates to `UtmParameters::MAX_VALUE_LENGTH`
(255) and turns empty results into `null`. Non-string values are dropped.

### ClickIds

Whitelisted advertising click identifiers.

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\ClickIds;

ClickIds::empty();
$ids = ClickIds::fromArray(['gclid' => 'abc', 'fbclid' => 'def']);

$ids->get(string $key): ?string;
$ids->has(string $key): bool;
$ids->isEmpty(): bool;
$ids->count(): int;
$ids->equals(ClickIds $other): bool;
$ids->toArray(): array;   // whitelist order
$ids->toJson(): string;   // '{}' when empty
```

`ClickIds::KNOWN_KEYS`: `gclid`, `gbraid`, `wbraid`, `fbclid`, `yclid`,
`ttclid`, `msclkid`, `li_fat_id`, `twclid`. Values must match
`/^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+\z/` and be at most 255 bytes. Serialised length is capped
at `MAX_SERIALIZED_LENGTH` (500) by dropping trailing keys.

### Referrer

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\Referrer;

$referrer = Referrer::of('https://ads.example.com/landing');  // ?Referrer
$referrer->url; $referrer->host;                              // host lowercased
$referrer->isInternal('shop.example.com'): bool;
$referrer->equals(Referrer $other): bool;

Referrer::external($sanitizedUrl, $currentHost): ?Referrer;   // null if internal
```

Takes an **already sanitised** absolute URL; returns `null` for relative URLs,
empty input, a URL longer than 500 characters, or any scheme other than `http`
and `https` — `javascript:`, `data:` and `file:` are rejected here rather than
in the capture layer, because this factory is also the gate a cookie and a
stored row pass through. All three capture sources
call `Referrer::external()`, not `Referrer::of()`: a referrer from the current
site itself (same host as the request) is navigation, not a touchpoint to
attribute the visit to.

### UtmTouchpoint

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\UtmTouchpoint;

$touchpoint = UtmTouchpoint::of(
    utm: $utm,
    occurredAt: new DateTimeImmutable('now', new DateTimeZone('UTC')),
    clickIds: $ids,          // optional, defaults to ClickIds::empty()
    referrer: $referrer,     // optional
    landingPage: 'https://shop.example.com/summer',  // optional
);

$touchpoint->isEmpty(): bool;                    // no utm, no click id, no referrer
$touchpoint->withOccurredAt(DateTimeImmutable): UtmTouchpoint;
```

Landing page is trimmed and truncated to 500 characters.

### UtmHistory

Ordered collection, newest first. `IteratorAggregate`, `Countable`.

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\{UtmHistory, UtmSimilarity};

UtmHistory::empty();
$history = UtmHistory::of($first, $second);
$history = $history->with($touchpoint);

$history->deduplicated(UtmSimilarity::Campaign);  // keeps the OLDEST of a group
$history->limited(5);                             // keeps the newest five
$history->latest(): ?UtmTouchpoint;
$history->oldest(): ?UtmTouchpoint;
$history->all(): array;   // list<UtmTouchpoint>
$history->count(): int;
$history->isEmpty(): bool;
```

### UtmSimilarity

```php
UtmSimilarity::Full;          // campaign tuple + click ids
UtmSimilarity::Campaign;      // source + medium + campaign
UtmSimilarity::SourceMedium;  // source + medium

$similarity->isSimilar(UtmTouchpoint $a, UtmTouchpoint $b): bool;  // reflexive, symmetric
```

### InteractionType

Validated string, not an enum — a library cannot know a consumer's events.

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\InteractionType;

InteractionType::registration();
InteractionType::purchase();
InteractionType::of('trial_started');   // /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}\z/, throws InvalidArgumentException
$type->value; $type->equals($other); (string) $type;
```

### Channel and ChannelResolver

Derived on read, never stored.

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\{Channel, ChannelResolver, DefaultChannelResolver};

$channel = (new DefaultChannelResolver())->resolve($touchpoint);
```

`Channel`: `Paid`, `Organic`, `Social`, `Email`, `Referral`, `Direct`, `Other`.

Rule order: any click id → `Paid`; then `utm_medium` against the paid, email,
social vocabularies plus literal `organic`/`referral`; then referrer host
against social and search host lists; no campaign and no referrer → `Direct`.
Vocabularies are constructor arguments (`paidMediums`, `emailMediums`,
`socialMediums`, `socialHosts`, `searchHosts`), each defaulting to a public
constant of the class.

### LandingPageSanitizer

```php
interface LandingPageSanitizer
{
    public function sanitize(string $url): string;  // '' when nothing is left
}
```

`DefaultLandingPageSanitizer` is the shipped implementation: it keeps scheme,
host, port and path, drops the fragment and every query parameter outside its
allow-list (`utm_*` and click ids by default), and truncates to 500 characters.
Non-http(s) schemes and relative URLs sanitise to an empty string.

Truncation cuts on a boundary the sanitizer can read back: a whole query pair,
never inside a percent-triplet, never leaving a dangling `?` or the `:` of a
port whose digits did not fit. That is what makes
`sanitize(sanitize($url)) === sanitize($url)` hold — the guarantee only assumes
`maxLength` still admits `scheme://` plus one character of the host.

### UtmAttribution

Immutable command. `fingerprint` and `dedupeKey` are computed in the
constructor and cannot be supplied.

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\UtmAttribution;

$attribution = new UtmAttribution(
    entityId: 'user-42',        // non-empty, <= 191 bytes, application-owned
    eventId: 'order-7',         // idempotency key, same constraints
    interactionType: InteractionType::purchase(),
    touchpoint: $touchpoint,
);

$attribution->fingerprint;  // sha256 of entity + type + campaign + click ids + landing page + referrer host
$attribution->dedupeKey;    // sha256(eventId . "\0" . fingerprint)
```

Invalid identifiers throw `Exception\InvalidUtmValue` (extends
`InvalidArgumentException`, implements `Exception\UtmException`). `occurredAt`
does not affect either hash.

### UtmAttributionRepository

Storage contract. Not bound by the core — implemented by
`rasuvaeff/yii3-utm-db` or by the application.

```php
public function append(UtmAttribution $attribution): bool;                  // false when the dedupe key existed
public function findByEntity(string $entityId, ?InteractionType $type = null, int $limit = 100, int $offset = 0): array;
public function findFirst(string $entityId, ?InteractionType $type = null): ?UtmAttributionRecord;
public function findLast(string $entityId, ?InteractionType $type = null): ?UtmAttributionRecord;
public function countByEntity(string $entityId, ?InteractionType $type = null): int;
public function deleteByEntity(string $entityId): int;                      // personal-data erasure
public function purgeOlderThan(DateTimeImmutable $before): int;             // retention
public function countOlderThan(DateTimeImmutable $before): int;             // what purgeOlderThan() would remove, for a dry run
```

`append()` must be race-safe (upsert-do-nothing, or insert with duplicate-key
handling). Reads return records in canonical order — `recordedAt`, then `id` —
both assigned by the server.

`UtmAttributionRecord`: `id(): string`, `attribution(): UtmAttribution`,
`recordedAt(): DateTimeImmutable`.

`InMemoryUtmAttributionRepository(ClockInterface $clock)` is a shipped
reference implementation for tests, returning `InMemoryUtmAttributionRecord`
instances. It is never bound in the container.

### UtmAttributionService

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\{UtmAttributionEvent, UtmAttributionService, UtmSimilarity};

$service = new UtmAttributionService(
    repository: $repository,
    similarity: UtmSimilarity::Full,   // how history is collapsed
    maxTouchpoints: 5,
);

$created = $service->record(new UtmAttributionEvent(
    entityId: 'user-42',
    eventId: 'order-7',
    interactionType: InteractionType::purchase(),
    history: $history,
));
```

Collapses history by similarity, caps it, writes oldest touchpoint first, one
row per surviving touchpoint, and returns how many rows were created. Empty
touchpoints are skipped. No transaction wraps the batch: per-touchpoint
deduplication makes a partial write self-healing on redelivery.

`UtmAttributionEventHandler(UtmAttributionService $service)` is an `__invoke`
listener. The package never subscribes it — wiring is the application's job.

### Capture stack

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\{BodyUtmSource, CookieUtmHistoryStore, HeaderUtmSource,
    NullUtmHistoryStore, QueryUtmSource, UtmCaptureMiddleware, UtmCookieCodec};

$middleware = new UtmCaptureMiddleware(
    sources: [new QueryUtmSource($clock, $sanitizer)],   // first non-null wins
    store: new CookieUtmHistoryStore(codec: new UtmCookieCodec(), clock: $clock),
    clock: $clock,
    consentPolicy: new AllowAllConsentPolicy(),
    similarity: UtmSimilarity::Full,
    ignoredPaths: [],
    maxTouchpoints: 5,
    maxTouchpointAge: UtmCaptureMiddleware::DEFAULT_MAX_TOUCHPOINT_AGE,  // 90 days
    enabled: true,
    updateExisting: false,
    captureOrganic: false,
    clearHistoryWithoutConsent: false,
);
```

`ignoredPaths` matches on a segment boundary — the path itself or anything
below it. `/api` skips `/api` and `/api/v1` and leaves `/api-docs` alone.

The cookie is rewritten only when the history changes, which keeps an unchanged
response cacheable and makes `ttlDays` count from the last touchpoint, not from
the last visit: a visitor returning daily through a direct link still loses the
history 30 days after the last campaign touch.

Request attributes (always set, `UtmAttributes::CURRENT|HISTORY|EFFECTIVE`):

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Utm\UtmRequest;

UtmRequest::current($request);    // ?UtmTouchpoint
UtmRequest::history($request);    // UtmHistory, possibly empty
UtmRequest::effective($request);  // ?UtmTouchpoint — current ?? history->latest()
```

Sources: `QueryUtmSource` (query string + landing page + `Referer`),
`HeaderUtmSource` (`X-Utm-Source` … `X-Utm-Id`, `X-Utm-Click-Ids`,
`X-Utm-Landing-Page`, `X-Utm-Referrer`, `X-Utm-Occurred-At`), `BodyUtmSource`
(nested `utm` key only — a flat body would turn unrelated form fields into
attribution data). Implement `UtmSource::extract()` for anything else.

`X-Utm-Click-Ids` is a JSON object, for example
`{"gclid":"...","fbclid":"..."}`. Invalid JSON degrades to empty click
ids. Query UTM/click-id keys, header prefix, body key and allowed click-id
subsets are constructor arguments and config-plugin params.

Stores: `CookieUtmHistoryStore` — one cookie for the whole history, `HttpOnly`
`Secure` `SameSite=Lax` for 30 days by default; `NullUtmHistoryStore` — stores
nothing, keeps responses cacheable. `read()`, `write()`, `forget()`.

`UtmCookieCodec` — `{"v":1,"t":[…]}`, `at` as a Unix timestamp. Decoding never
throws: a foreign version, malformed JSON, an oversized value or a broken entry
yields an empty history. Decoding also re-sanitises `r` and `lp` through a
`LandingPageSanitizer` (constructor argument, second): a cookie is exactly as
untrusted as a query string. Encoding drops the oldest touchpoints until
`strlen(urlencode($value))` fits `maxLength` (3500 by default) — the budget is
spent on the percent-encoded value, because that is what `Set-Cookie` carries
and what the 4096-byte browser limit applies to.

`TouchpointTime` (internal) parses a claimed timestamp — Unix or any format
`DateTimeImmutable` accepts, falling back to the clock. `withinWindow()` caps a
future claim to `now` and returns `null` for a claim older than
`maxTouchpointAge`; the middleware drops such a touchpoint from the history and
rewrites the cookie. Moving a stale claim to the window boundary instead would
invent a timestamp and keep the touchpoint alive forever.

### Consent

```php
interface ConsentPolicy
{
    public function allowsPersistence(ServerRequestInterface $request): bool;
}
```

`AllowAllConsentPolicy` (default) and `CallbackConsentPolicy`. Without consent
the middleware reads nothing, writes nothing, and still sets empty attributes.
The method name matches `rasuvaeff/yii3-ab-testing-web` on purpose.

### Configuration

`config/di.php` binds the codec, `LandingPageSanitizer`, `ChannelResolver`,
`ConsentPolicy`, `UtmHistoryStore`, `UtmCaptureMiddleware`,
`UtmAttributionService` and `UtmAttributionEventHandler`. It does **not** bind
`UtmAttributionRepository` — exactly one source may, or `yiisoft/config` throws
`Duplicate key`. It subscribes no events either.

`config/params.php` → `rasuvaeff/yii3-utm` with `capture`, `sanitizer`,
`channel`, `cookie` and `attribution` sections. `capture.sources` configures
query keys, click-id subsets, header prefix and body key; `sanitizer` configures
the query allow-list/limit; `channel` configures resolver vocabularies.
